worked.title: Q1 · Rank, column space, subspace (7 marks)

problem.text: A = [[1, 0, 0, 1], [2, −1, 0, 1], [0, −2, −2, −4], [0, 1, 1, 2]]. (a) Rank of A. [3M] (b) W = column space of A: basis and dimension. [2M] (c) Show U = {r(1, 1, −2, 1) : r ∈ ℝ} is a subspace of W. [2M]

steps.label: (b)
steps.text: Pivots in columns 1, 2, 3 ⇒ basis of W = the original columns {(1, 2, 0, 0), (0, −1, −2, 1), (0, 0, −2, 1)}, **dim W = 3**. (Column 4 = column 1 + column 2 + column 3.)

steps.label: (c) Subspace
steps.text: 0 ∈ U (r = 0); r₁v + r₂v = (r₁ + r₂)v ∈ U; c(rv) = (cr)v ∈ U. So U is a subspace of W.

worked.answer: rank 3; W has basis {c₁, c₂, c₃}, dim 3; (1, 1, −2, 1) = c₁ + c₂, so U is a subspace of W.
worked.priorityWhy: Recent paper: sit it as a timed mock (≈ 3.4 min per mark)

worked.title: Q2 · SVD; covariance and the direction of maximum variance (7 marks)

problem.text: A = [[−2, 0], [1, 1], [1, −1]]. (a) SVD A = UΣVᵀ. [4M] (b) Treat the rows of A as sample data: eigenvalues of the covariance matrix and the direction of maximum variance. [3M]

steps.label: (a) U
steps.text: u₁ = Av₁/σ₁ = (−2, 1, 1)/√6; u₂ = Av₂/σ₂ = (0, 1, −1)/√2; u₃ completes the basis: (1, 1, 1)/√3.

steps.label: (b) Centre
steps.text: Row mean = (0, 0): the data is already centred.

steps.label: (b) Covariance
steps.text: Sample covariance AᵀA/(N − 1) = [[3, 0], [0, 1]] ⇒ eigenvalues **3 and 1** (with 1/N: 2 and 2/3; state which you use).

worked.answer: σ = √6, √2 with U = [(−2, 1, 1)/√6, (0, 1, −1)/√2, (1, 1, 1)/√3], V = I; covariance eigenvalues 3, 1; maximum variance along (1, 0).
worked.priorityWhy: Recent paper: sit it as a timed mock (≈ 3.4 min per mark)

worked.title: Q3 · Chain rule; constrained problem and its dual (6 marks)

problem.text: (a) w = xy + yz + xz with x = u + v, y = u² − v, z = u − v². Find ∂w/∂u and ∂w/∂v. [3M] (b) Receiver cost 3(x² + y²); region R: x + y − 1 ≥ 0, x + y − 3 ≤ 0. (i) Formulate the problem. [1M] (ii) Its Lagrangian dual. [2M]

steps.label: (b)(i)
steps.text: min 3(x² + y²) s.t. 1 − x − y ≤ 0, x + y − 3 ≤ 0.

steps.label: (b)(ii) Lagrangian
steps.text: L = 3x² + 3y² + λ₁(1 − x − y) + λ₂(x + y − 3), λ₁, λ₂ ≥ 0. ∂L/∂x = 0 ⇒ x = (λ₁ − λ₂)/6, the same for y.

steps.label: (b)(ii) Dual
steps.text: Substituting: D(λ₁, λ₂) = −(λ₁ − λ₂)²/6 + λ₁ − 3λ₂. Dual: **max D s.t. λ₁, λ₂ ≥ 0**. (Check: optimum λ = (3, 0), D = 1.5 = primal cost at (½, ½).)

worked.answer: ∂w/∂u = 6u² + 2u − v − v² + 2uv − 2uv²; ∂w/∂v = u² − u − 2v − 2v(u² + u); dual max −(λ₁ − λ₂)²/6 + λ₁ − 3λ₂, λ ≥ 0.
worked.priorityWhy: Recent paper: sit it as a timed mock (≈ 3.4 min per mark)

worked.title: Q4 · Momentum versus plain GD (7 marks)

problem.text: f(x, y) = (x − 1)² + (y − 1)², start (1.5, 1.5), α = 0.05, β = 0.8. Two momentum iterations (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂); two plain GD iterations (a₁, b₁), (a₂, b₂). Is momentum better?

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Running momentum and plain GD side by side for two iterations, then a one-line conclusion about which is better.

steps.label: Plan of attack
steps.text: 1. Write both update rules. 2. Find ∇f once. 3. Momentum: for each iteration, gradient at the current point → new velocity → new position. 4. Plain GD: gradient → new position. 5. Compare distances (or f) to the minimum and conclude.

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: This paper's symbols are kept: **α = 0.05 is the step size** (η on the lecture boards), β = 0.8 is the momentum, (x, y) for momentum and (a, b) for plain GD.

steps.label: STEP 1 · Update rules
steps.text:
Momentum: vₜ₊₁ = βvₜ − α∇f(xₜ), xₜ₊₁ = xₜ + vₜ₊₁, v₀ = (0, 0).
Plain GD: aₜ₊₁ = aₜ − α∇f(aₜ).

steps.label: STEP 2 · Gradient
steps.text: ∂f/∂x = 2(x − 1), ∂f/∂y = 2(y − 1). Minimum at (1, 1). f and the start (1.5, 1.5) are symmetric in x and y, so both coordinates always move together.

steps.label: STEP 12 · Why compare
steps.text:
The last part of the question asks: **is there any advantage of momentum?** To answer with numbers instead of a guess, measure **how close each method got to the minimum** after two iterations.
This is **not** an MSE: there is no data here. We only use the question's own function f.

steps.label: STEP 13 · Measure 1: gap to the minimum
steps.text:
f(x, y) = (x − 1)² + (y − 1)² is smallest at **(1, 1)**.
• Momentum is at (1.365, 1.365): gap = 1.365 − 1 = **0.365** in each coordinate.
• Plain GD is at (1.405, 1.405): gap = 1.405 − 1 = **0.405** in each coordinate.
Smaller gap = closer ⇒ momentum is closer.

steps.label: STEP 14 · Measure 2: value of f
steps.text:
Evaluate the question's f at each point: this says how high we still are on the bowl (the lowest value is 0, at (1, 1)).
Since x = y here, f = (x − 1)² + (x − 1)² = 2(x − 1)².
• Start (1.5, 1.5): f = 2 × 0.5² = 2 × 0.25 = **0.5**
• Momentum (1.365, 1.365): f = 2 × 0.365² = 2 × 0.133225 = **0.2665**
• Plain GD (1.405, 1.405): f = 2 × 0.405² = 2 × 0.164025 = **0.3281**
Lower f = closer to the minimum ⇒ momentum is lower.

steps.label: STEP 15 · Conclude
steps.text:
**Yes, momentum helps.** Both measures agree: after two iterations momentum is closer to (1, 1) (gap 0.365 vs 0.405) and has the lower f (0.2665 vs 0.3281).
Why: the two methods agree in iteration 1 (v₀ = 0). From iteration 2 momentum adds β × v₁ = 0.8 × (−0.05) = −0.04, the extra distance it covers.
Exam tip: one measure is enough to support the conclusion; the gaps are quicker to write.

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• Forgetting that iteration 1 is identical for both.
• Dropping βv₁ in iteration 2.
• Concluding without numbers: state the gaps 0.365 vs 0.405.

worked.answer: Momentum: (1.45, 1.45), (1.365, 1.365); plain GD: (1.45, 1.45), (1.405, 1.405); momentum converges faster.

worked.title: Q5 · Soft margin: compare two models (7 marks)

problem.text: x₁ (0, 0) −1, x₂ (2, 2) +1, x₃ (2, 0) −1, x₄ (0, 2) +1; C = 1. A: w = (1, 1), b = −1.5. B: w = (1, −1), b = 0. (a) ½‖w‖². (b) Hinge losses and sums. (c) Objectives; better model. (d) Margin errors and correct points of the better model.

steps.label: (d)
steps.text: x₃ misclassified, x₄ inside the margin; x₁, x₂, x₄ correctly classified.

worked.answer: A: 3, B: 9; A is better; x₃ misclassified, x₄ a margin error.
